transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining this curriculum-approval meeting. As you know, the partner high school has proposed a dual-credit environmental science course for the spring term, and I have final authority to approve the course and its operating details. Before I sign off on anything, I need each of you to report any information that must be reflected in the proposal before approval. The draft currently lists a maximum enrollment of 28 students, three credits, and Ms. Patel as the instructor. Please share anything I need to know.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag a concern before approval. I inspected the planned laboratory room and found that the room's fixed workstations and required aisle clearance allow no more than 20 students for this course. I recorded the measurement in my classroom notes but haven't yet attached it to the curriculum proposal. The draft lists a maximum enrollment of 28, but the physical space can only safely accommodate 20.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag a discrepancy before approval. My transcript crosswalk, which I confirmed with the community-college records office, requires this dual-credit course to use the exact course code ENV-115 and carry exactly 4 college credits. The draft proposal currently lists three credits, and neither the course code nor the correct credit value has been entered in the high-school scheduling system yet. These details must be corrected before approval is signed.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag a critical issue before approval. The signed articulation memorandum on file in my partnership records requires me, Dr. Lewis, to teach the first six weeks of the inaugural offering of this course. This memorandum was not included with the draft proposal, but it is a binding requirement that must be reflected before approval is signed.
